title.narrative: Increased Resilience of communities to engage in Violence, Ninewa Governorate

description.narrative: In the aftermath of the violence committed by Islamic State – Daesh (IS), a lack of social cohesion, deep rifts within and between communities and the exclusion of minorities from peace processes create fertile ground for renewed violence in Iraq’s Ninewa governorate. With the support of the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) has been implementing the first phase of a project focused on establishing community peace teams, existing of women and youth, to increase trust within and between communities, including with duty bearers. So far, the project made important progress in doing exactly that, focusing on the relationships within and between Sinjar and Ba’aj communities, as well as the increased responsiveness of duty bearers that has improved engagement and trust in the former to address community needs. Based on lessons learned from phase 1, the proposed phase of the project focuses on strengthening social bonds between and across these communities and expanding the opportunities for civilians and duty bearers to jointly address challenges related to stabilisation. Important lessons learned are related to Community Peace Team (CPT) sustainability; the importance of common spaces to connect in; and the need to create an inclusive network of youth and women beyond Sinjar and Ba’aj districts. In response, NP will extend its programming in Ninewa, moving towards this diverse network of CPTs across ethnic-religious, returnee-host community, and tribal divides. NP will do so through incorporating existing CPTs already established in Tel Afar district into its programming and by organising multiple dialogues and conferences with CPTs, other civil society members and duty bearers in Ninewa Governorate. In doing so, NP seeks to enhance the sustainability of its actions and work towards social cohesion in Iraq’s most ethnically diverse Governorate and lowest social cohesion. Ultimately, the project will contribute to violence prevention by increasing the resilience of communities to refrain from engaging in violent ways to address conflict and divisive narratives. The project incorporates innovative methods to address harmful gender norms and divisive narratives that may incite violence online and in the physical context. In doing so, the communities themselves, together with duty bearers and NP, intend to contribute to sustainable peace and stability in the region.

Main Objective: Increased resilience of Ninewa communities to engage in violence.SO1: Community Peace Teams are well positioned to engage with duty bearers and take initiative to enhance social cohesion. SO2: Peace and security processes are more inclusive of diverse civilians’ voices, and duty bearers are more responsive to community needs in Ninewa Governorate. SO3: A more conducive and safer environment is created for community members to address barriers to social cohesion.
